title: What the Python SDK's ZDX results contain: envelopes, missing fields and paging

prose.text: The Python ZDX methods turn each response into model objects whose attributes mirror the API's snake_case keys. How they get there decides which attributes survive.

prose.label: Narrow models.

checks.do: Whether a field that comes back None from a Python ZDX object has a multiword key; read it from the raw response (`response.get_body()`) instead.
Whether a paged Python ZDX listing was walked with the response object's `next()`, which yields no records; pass `next_offset` as `offset` by hand.

list-envelopes.statement: List methods such as `list_ongoing`, `list_historical`, `list_devices` and `list_users` wrap the whole response body in one envelope object (`Alerts`, `Devices`, `ActiveUsers`) and return it as a one-element list.

def list_users(self, query_params: Optional[dict] = None) -> APIResult[List[ActiveUsers]]:
result = [ActiveUsers(self.form_response_body(response.get_body()))]

models-read-snake.statement: The ZDX models look their fields up under the API's snake_case keys (for example `trace_id` in `DeviceDeepTraces`, `next_offset` in `Devices`, `total_users` in `ActiveApplications`), and methods such as `get_deeptrace` and `list_apps` build the models from `form_response_body` of the response.

self.next_offset = config["next_offset"] if "next_offset" in config else None
self.total_users = config["total_users"] if "total_users" in config else None

result = [DeviceDeepTraces(self.form_response_body(response.get_body()))]

multiword-attrs-lost.statement: So on those methods every model attribute whose API key has more than one word (a deep trace's `trace_id`, a device list's `next_offset`, an application's `total_users`, and the like) comes back None, and the MCP tools that return these models' records omit those fields; single-word keys such as `id`, `name` and `score` survive.
multiword-attrs-lost.conditions: Follows from the camel-casing helper and the models' snake_case lookups at the pin; no recorded ZDX response at the pin shows it, and the ZDX integration tests that would read these fields are commented out.

raw-exceptions.statement: A few methods skip that conversion: `list_deeptraces` and `get_call_quality_metrics` build their models from the raw response items, and `list_softwares` hands the raw body to its `SoftwareList` wrapper.

most-impacted-region.statement: The Python `MostImpactedRegion` model reads only `id` and `country`, while the contract's `most_impacted_region` also carries `city`, `region`, `state`, `geo_type`, coordinates and detection details.

quotes: if config: self.id = config["id"] if "id" in config else None self.country = config["country"] if "country" in config else None else: self.id = None self.country = None
def __init__(self, config: Optional[Any] = None) -> None: pass

most-impacted-region.conditions: The two quoted assignments are every attribute the model's constructor sets at the pin.

call-quality-strings.statement: The Python `CallQualityMetrics` model forms its `metrics` as a list of `str`, which turns each metric object into its string form, while the contract defines each element as a `Series` object of `metric`, `unit` and `datapoints`.

quotes: self.metrics = ZscalerCollection.form_list(config["metrics"] if "metrics" in config else [], str)
collection[index] = data_type(collection[index])

call-quality-strings.conditions: Follows from `form_list` calling `str()` on each non-string element; the Go SDK's `[]common.Metric` matches the contract's object shape.

paging.statement: The Python response object pages ZDX lists by `next_offset`: `has_next()` is true while a `next_offset` is present, the next request sends it as `offset`, and each page's records are read from the body's `items` key.

quotes: self._list = self._body.get("items", [])
self._next_offset = self._body.get("next_offset")
self._params["offset"] = self._next_offset
has_next = self._next_offset is not None

paging-reads-items.statement: No paged ZDX list response in the contract has an `items` key (they hold `alerts`, `devices`, `users` or `software` beside `next_offset`), so `next()` on a ZDX response returns no records and callers have to pass `next_offset` back as `offset` themselves.

next_offset.description: This value must be entered in the next request to get the next batch from the list.

paging-reads-items.conditions: A search of the contract's ZDX responses that carry `next_offset` (ongoing and historical alerts, affected devices, devices, app users, users and both software inventory reads) finds none with `items`; not observed against a live tenant.

python-device-list-fields.statement: The Python `list_devices` returns a `Devices` wrapper whose `devices` list is formed of `DeviceDetail` objects, which read only `id`, `name` and `userid`; the contract's device-list entries also carry fields such as `os`, `hw_model`, `private_ip` and `client_conn_ver`.

def list_devices(self, query_params: Optional[dict] = None) -> APIResult[List[Devices]]:

call-quality-shape.title: The live shape of each call-quality `metrics` element
call-quality-shape.detail: The contract defines each element as a `Series` object, matching the Go SDK; the Python model stringifies the elements. No captured live response confirms the contract's shape.
